detection.notes: Archived bagakit-ft rows remain historical implementation evidence. The active backlog is now a manual review-derived follow-up plan refreshed on 2026-03-24 after re-reading the kernel architecture/backlog docs, re-checking targeted package coverage (`pkg/builtin` 66.8%, `pkg/service/httpapi` 71.1%, `pkg/engine/runtime` 87.1%), and observing repeated low-space interruptions in the default evidence gate.

rows.title: Restore lint/check gate and remove stale orchestrator helpers
rows.why_now: `make check` is currently red on staticcheck findings, so the project's default evidence gate is already broken before any new kernel work begins.
acceptance_criteria: `make lint` exits 0 with no SA1012/SA4000/U1000 findings.
`make check` exits 0 after the cleanup.
The fixed assertions still verify the intended behavior instead of weakening test coverage.
evidence: `go test ./pkg/adapter/localfs ./pkg/engine` passes after switching the localfs helper test to a non-canceled context and tightening the JSONL assertion to path plus file kind.
`make lint` exits 0 after removing the duplicated assertion and the three caller-free orchestrator helpers.
`make check` exits 0, restoring the repository's default gate with both tests and staticcheck green.
risks: Keep the change surgical: restore the gate without changing command-dispatch semantics.
If any removed helper is still conceptually needed, reintroduce it only with a live call site and regression coverage.

rows.title: Add direct package tests for agentfs zone behavior and pathguard escapes
rows.why_now: The default workspace trust story depends on `agentfs` and `pathguard`, but those packages still have zero direct package coverage even though they own zone resolution and path-escape prevention.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs ./pkg/adapter/internal/pathguard` passes with new direct tests.
Tests cover writable vs read-only zones, path normalization, metadata shaping, and symlink or missing-ancestor escape rejection.
Integration sanity remains green under `go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine`.
evidence: `pkg/adapter/agentfs/filespace_core_test.go` covers root-zone listing, `PathEnv()` normalization and dedupe, read-write vs read-only `DescribePath()` metadata, read-only write preflight, and direct plus nested symlink escape rejection through package-local helpers.

`pkg/adapter/internal/pathguard/pathguard_test.go` covers safe missing descendants, direct and nested symlink escape rejection, and `resolveWithExistingPrefix()` preserving the unresolved suffix after resolving an existing symlink ancestor.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs ./pkg/adapter/internal/pathguard` and `go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine` both exit 0 on the 2026-03-24 rerun.
risks: Avoid duplicating the full integration harness; target the low-level invariants that can regress silently.
If direct tests expose a real bug, patch the production code in the same smallest closure instead of papering over the failure.

rows.title: Harden parser and redirection regressions around heredoc and edge-case script syntax
rows.why_now: The parser and script runner are core kernel surfaces, but heredoc branches and several parser failure paths remain effectively unexercised, which makes shell-level regressions easy to miss.
acceptance_criteria: New engine tests cover heredoc success plus failure cases such as missing delimiters or unclosed quotes.
Redirection edge tests cover write or append behavior without introducing partial side effects or unexpected exit-code changes.
`go test ./pkg/engine ./pkg/sh` passes, and `go test ./...` stays green.
evidence: `pkg/engine/engine_test.go` now covers heredoc success through `eng.Execute(...)`, parser failures for missing delimiter, unterminated heredoc, and unclosed quote, plus heredoc-driven append and write-limited redirection behavior without partial side effects.
`go test ./pkg/engine ./pkg/sh` exits 0 after the new regression coverage is added.
An initial `go test ./...` hit `go: creating work dir ... no space left on device`; after `go clean -cache -testcache` freed Go build cache space, the rerun of `go test ./...` exited 0.
risks: Keep the shell surface stable; start with tests and only change semantics when a failing regression proves the need.
Do not broaden shell compatibility beyond the documented subset while adding coverage.

rows.title: Close regression gaps in HTTP and CLI entry surfaces
rows.why_now: Entry adapters are not the architecture center, but they are still public integration surfaces; current coverage misses serve-mode branches, service wrappers, and include-meta fallback edges.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./cmd/simsh-cli ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` passes with new regression coverage.
Tests cover session error/status mapping and at least one `include_meta` path that exercises mount or synthetic-path metadata fallback behavior.
CLI tests cover serve-mode option normalization or root fallback without relying on a long-lived network listener.
evidence: `cmd/simsh-cli/main_test.go` adds a deterministic `runServe()` regression that uses the missing-port address `127.0.0.1`, asserts the cwd root fallback plus mount banner, and exits through `contract.ExitCodeGeneral` without opening a long-lived listener.

`pkg/service/httpapi/handler_test.go` adds direct helper coverage for `statusForSessionError()` and mounted-path fallback coverage for `describePathMetaViaLS()` via `/test/core-strict/cases/echo-basic.sh` with `EnableTestCorpus=true`.

`pkg/service/service_test.go` covers uninitialized service errors, the command-required fast path, `OpsFactory` error propagation, and a real-engine success path; `go test ./cmd/simsh-cli ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` and `make test` both exit 0.
risks: Keep tests deterministic and non-blocking; do not add network flake just to raise coverage.
If fallback metadata is dead code, either prove it with tests or remove it explicitly rather than leaving an unowned branch.

rows.title: Cover agentfs mutation and write-limit invariants directly
rows.why_now: The default workspace still depends on `agentfs` for trusted writes, but direct package coverage remains only 41.5% and every mutator path (`WriteFile`, `AppendFile`, `EditFile`, `MakeDir`, `RemoveFile`) is still uncovered.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs` passes with direct tests covering writable-zone writes/appends/edits/removes plus read-only rejection in `/knowledge_base`.
Tests prove write-limit failures reject oversize write, append, and edit payloads without leaving partial on-disk mutations.
`go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine` remains green so the low-level coverage hardening preserves integrated runtime behavior.
evidence: `pkg/adapter/agentfs/filespace_core_test.go` now directly covers writable-zone `WriteFile`, `AppendFile`, `EditFile`, `MakeDir`, and `RemoveFile` behavior, including host-path assertions and directory-removal rejection.
The same direct suite proves `/knowledge_base` rejects write, append, edit, mkdir, and remove mutations with `contract.ErrUnsupported` while preserving pre-existing file content.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs` and `go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine` both exited 0 on the 2026-03-24 rerun after adding no-partial-mutation checks for oversize write, append, and edit failures.
risks: If a new direct test exposes a production bug, fix the filesystem semantics in the same closure instead of weakening the assertion.
Keep the scope at package-local invariants; do not duplicate the larger integration suite already owned by `pkg/fs` and `pkg/engine`.

rows.title: Cover agentfs search and path-resolution edge cases
rows.why_now: Agent inspect/search loops rely on `agentfs` path normalization and search expansion, but `RequireAbsolutePath`, `ResolveSearchPaths`, `CollectFilesUnder`, `toVirtualPath`, and `NewDefaultFilesystem` are still uncovered direct behavior.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs` passes with direct tests for `RequireAbsolutePath`, file-vs-directory `ResolveSearchPaths`, recursive root search, and `CollectFilesUnder` sorted cross-zone output.
Tests cover `toVirtualPath`/zone-root normalization and prove search/path results stay rooted under allowed zones only.
`go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine/runtime` remains green after the new search/path regressions are added.
evidence: `pkg/adapter/agentfs/filespace_core_test.go` now directly covers `RequireAbsolutePath`, file-vs-directory `ResolveSearchPaths`, missing zone-local targets, recursive root search, sorted cross-zone `CollectFilesUnder`, `toVirtualPath`, and deterministic `NewDefaultFilesystem` cwd fallback plus zone layout.

`pkg/adapter/agentfs/filespace_core.go` now checks host-path existence inside `ResolveSearchPaths`, so a missing file under an allowed zone returns `No such file or directory` instead of being surfaced as a searchable file path.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs` and `go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine/runtime` both exited 0 on the 2026-03-24 rerun after the new search/path regressions landed.
risks: Avoid coupling tests to incidental helper ordering beyond the documented sorted-output contract.
If search-path behavior is unclear, tighten the contract in tests first and only then change production code.

rows.title: Add deterministic smoke coverage for TUI and simshd entry wrappers
rows.why_now: Entry surfaces are downstream from the kernel, but they are still public operator paths; `pkg/cmd` and `cmd/simshd` both remain at 0.0% package coverage, so launcher drift can go unnoticed until manual use.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/cmd ./cmd/simshd ./cmd/simsh-cli` passes with deterministic tests that exercise console-model render/state transitions without needing a real TTY.

The `simshd` launcher is covered through a testable helper or equivalent seam that validates root fallback, profile/policy parsing, and listen-address normalization without holding a long-lived listener open.
The new tests preserve the documented architecture rule that CLI/TUI and HTTP wrappers stay thin over shared runtime code.
evidence: `pkg/cmd/console_tui_test.go` now covers `newConsoleModel(...)`, `Update(...)`, and `View()` state transitions, including loading-to-resized rendering, blank input, `exit`/`quit`, command dispatch via `tea.BatchMsg`, `executeResultMsg` handling, and `Ctrl+L` transcript clearing without starting a real Bubble Tea program.

`cmd/simshd/main.go` now routes through a package-local `flag.NewFlagSet` launcher seam, and `cmd/simshd/main_test.go` validates cwd root fallback, invalid profile or policy rejection, `-P` overriding `-listen`, and `EnableTestMount` wiring into `httpapi.Config` with a stubbed serve path.
`go test ./pkg/cmd ./cmd/simshd ./cmd/simsh-cli` and `make test` both exited 0 on 2026-03-24 after the new entry-surface regression coverage landed.
risks: Keep tests model-level and deterministic; avoid flaky terminal or network integration coverage just to move the percentage.
If testability requires refactoring, extract thin seams instead of pushing more runtime logic into entry commands.

rows.title: Close `ls`/`man`/`json` edge-case regressions in the default workspace
rows.why_now: The default workspace is the agent's main surface, yet `pkg/builtin` still sits at 66.8% coverage and the least-covered logic is concentrated in `ls`, `man`, and `json`, which drive directory inspection, command discovery, and structured querying.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/builtin ./pkg/engine` passes with new regression coverage for recursive or formatted listing paths, `man --list` text or external fallback behavior, and `json stat/get` directory plus invalid-argument branches.

Tests cover at least one `ls -R -l` path plus one `ls -l --fmt md|json` path that exercises metadata defaults or formatter fallback, so agent-visible listing contracts stop depending on mostly untested helpers.
The new coverage proves `json stat/get` keeps stable usage or general exit codes for invalid formats, directory targets, and expansion-no-files cases without weakening current happy-path behavior.
evidence: `pkg/builtin/coverage_test.go` now adds direct command-level regressions for `ls -R -l`, `ls -al --fmt md`, `man --list`, `json stat` invalid-format/no-files paths, and `json get` bad-flag/directory paths without widening builtin semantics.
`pkg/builtin/effective_core_additional_test.go` now covers `runManList("text")` with sorted builtin rows plus external blank-summary fallback rendering as `(no description)`.

Validation passed with `gofmt -w pkg/builtin/coverage_test.go pkg/builtin/effective_core_additional_test.go pkg/builtin/op_listing.go pkg/builtin/op_help_manual.go pkg/builtin/op_json.go`, `go test ./pkg/builtin -run 'TestBuiltinCommandCoverage|TestLSLongFormatHonorsCustomFormatterAndJSONDisplayPath|TestJSONFormattingHelpersAndTargetExpansion|TestManHelpers'`, `go test ./pkg/builtin ./pkg/engine`, and `go test ./pkg/builtin -cover`, with `pkg/builtin` coverage rising to 70.2%.
risks: Prefer tests first; only change builtin behavior if the new regressions expose a real contract bug.
Keep the surface dual-readable and additive; do not turn this closure into a second output-format redesign.
Default `ls` hidden-file visibility in recursive listings remains unchanged and is still an undocumented seam; this pass intentionally avoided freezing that behavior without a clearer contract.

rows.title: Harden session-manager lifecycle and adapter failure edges
rows.why_now: Session lifecycle is a core kernel contract, and `pkg/engine/runtime` still leaves the lowest coverage in `Execute` and `Resume` precisely where policy narrowing, adapter phases, and closed-session recovery interact.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference` passes with new tests for create, checkpoint, resume, or close adapter failures, blank or missing session ids, and runtime rebuild behavior after adapter-managed mounts change.
Tests prove adapter-phase failures do not partially rewrite session snapshot or checkpoint state, and closed or missing sessions keep returning stable typed errors.
Coverage for `pkg/engine/runtime` improves from the current 87.1% with direct exercise of the current low branches in `Execute`, `Resume`, and `invokeAdapterPhase`.
evidence: `pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager_test.go` now covers blank-id and blank-command handling, create/checkpoint/close/resume adapter failures, active-session resume no-op behavior, and read-only runtime rebuilds that keep adapter-projected `/memory` mounts available after failure.
`pkg/engine/runtime/runtime_core_additional_test.go` now rejects blank adapter IDs and unsupported adapter phases directly, lifting `applySessionAdapters` and `invokeAdapterPhase` coverage to 100.0%.

`pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager.go` now stages adapter mount updates until adapter hooks and any runtime rebuild both succeed, so observe/checkpoint/close failures no longer clear stored adapter mounts on the way out.

`go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -run 'TestSessionManager|TestApplySessionAdapters|TestInvokeAdapterPhase'`, `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference`, and `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -cover` all exit 0, and runtime coverage rises from 87.1% to 93.8%.
risks: The remaining uncovered `Execute` branches are mostly lock-loss or runtime-construction fault paths that need contrived injection rather than more lifecycle contract expansion.
Future adapters can still fail runtime reconstruction by returning invalid mounts; this pass preserves prior state on failure but does not add a broader mount-validation layer.

rows.title: Close HTTP execute or session metadata edge cases and request parsing gaps
rows.why_now: The HTTP integration surface still sits at 71.1% coverage, and code inspection shows `decodeOptionalJSON`, `describePathMeta`, and path extraction around `include_meta` are only partially exercised even though higher-level harnesses depend on them.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` passes with new tests for empty or null session POST bodies, invalid JSON bodies, metadata fallback or defaulting branches, and shell tokenization edge cases.

An explicit `include_meta` request that names `/` or other quoted or escaped absolute paths keeps the intended path in `meta.paths`, so metadata extraction matches the command the caller actually sent.
Coverage for `pkg/service/httpapi` improves from the current 71.1% while preserving existing success-path and session-lifecycle behavior.
evidence: `pkg/service/httpapi/handler_test.go` now covers empty and `null` session bodies, invalid execute JSON bodies, blank commands, session override rejection, direct `describePathMeta(...)` defaults, and explicit-root `include_meta` behavior.
`pkg/service/httpapi/execute_endpoint.go` now preserves explicit `/` tokens in `extractAbsPaths()` so `meta.paths` matches caller-named root paths without changing dedupe or sort behavior.
`go test ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` exits 0 after the regressions land.
`go test ./pkg/service/httpapi -cover` exits 0 and reports 79.3% coverage, up from 71.1%.
risks: Keep the handler thin; prefer small parsing or metadata fixes over pushing runtime semantics into HTTP-only code.
If root-path metadata is intentionally excluded, document and test that contract explicitly instead of leaving code and comments contradictory.

rows.title: Make long-run preflight resilient to transient temp-space failures
rows.why_now: The current long-run loop can misclassify actionable work as blocked when temporary-file creation fails transiently, and this repo is currently operating with less than 200 MiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`, which makes that noise recurring rather than hypothetical.
acceptance_criteria: `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` surfaces low-space or temp-file failures as a retryable preflight outcome with a deterministic hint instead of only a raw shell failure.
A rerun after a successful tiny-write sanity check keeps `next-action.json` and `feature-list.json` consistent instead of leaving the loop in a spurious no-next-action state.
`bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` or equivalent runner guidance documents the exact retry path for temp-space anomalies.
evidence: `make lint`, `make check`, and several package-local test runs in this session all failed at least once with `no space left on device` before succeeding again after cache cleanup or retry.

`docs/.bagakit/inbox/howto-long-run-preflight-rerun.md` already records a concrete initializer incident where a second `check_and_resume.sh` run selected the same row cleanly after a transient temp-file failure.
The generated `check_and_resume.sh` currently runs validation directly and stops on the first shell failure without classifying low-space issues as retryable loop noise.
risks: Keep the runner orchestration-only; do not bury project-specific repair logic inside long-run scripts.
If temp-space failures are actually durable, the new preflight must still stop the loop clearly instead of silently masking the problem.
